text: {"en":["These are the words of Yedidyah the Alexandrian [Philo] in his book on the times: from Adam to the Flood, one thousand six hundred and fifty-six years.","From the Flood to Abraham, two hundred and ninety-two. From Abraham to Moses, four hundred and twenty-five.","From Moses to the exodus of Israel from Egypt and the beginning of the Tabernacle of boards, eighty.","From the Tabernacle to the beginning of the building of the Temple of stone, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, and in accordance with David's command concerning the order of his sons who were to succeed him,","four hundred and eighty. For when a dispute arose among the sons born to David by Bathsheba (written in 2 Kings 5 and 1 Chronicles 3) as to which of them should take precedence after him, ⚠","he commanded that the succession begin with the youngest, and that when the one who began died without sons, the brother nearest to him in age should rise in his place.","And so it began with Solomon, the youngest of them all. After him the kingship was due to Nathan, who was born next to him,","for which reason he was called Ahi ha-Sar and Mattat (1 Kings 4), and his sons were called Ahei ha-Sarim and Mattatim, ⚠","because all of them were brothers of the prince and destined in the course of time to reign in his place.","From that time until Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah, the seed of Nathan was always called Ahei ha-Sarim,","and the men whom Jehoram killed, who were of the seed of Nathan (2 Chronicles 21: \"He had brothers, the sons of,\" etc.) and whom Jehoshaphat, Jehoram's father, had honored in the tribe of Judah beyond his father's command,","were called sons of Jehoshaphat and brothers of Jehoram. Likewise the sons (6) of the men whom Jehoram left in the tribe of Judah, though without rank of income, ⚠","were called sons and brothers of Ahaziah, although he was Jehoram's only son and he alone remained of the seed of Solomon.","Therefore, when he was killed, Athaliah strove to put to death all the royal seed of the Ahei ha-Sarim.","But through the cunning of Jehosheba, Ahaziah's sister, the youngest among the Ahei ha-Sarim was saved, he who was called Eli and also Eliakim,","for (7) among the Arameans and the Egyptians, Eli, Eliakim and Jehoiakim are interchangeable.","This one, who in his youth was called Eli, was Joash, the first of the seed of David [to reign] from the remnant of the seed of Nathan,","concerning whom the choirs of singers on the right and the left sang the psalm numbered by the Seventy Elders 74 (for us it is 75), composed at Jehoiada's direction, that (8) God should not utterly cut off the seed of the house of David now that the seed of Solomon had come to an end.","From this Joash onward, the kings are recorded by two names, even three,","for this first one was called Eli, Joash and Simeon,","and likewise Er Manasseh, Hezekiah Jeshua, and the like.","Thus from the fourth year of Solomon to the end of his seed and the first to rise from the Ahei ha-Sarim, called Joash, one hundred and thirty-eight years elapsed.","From Joash to the exile, I mean that of Jehoiachin, two hundred and ninety-one years elapsed,","including ten years in which Amon reigned while Er Manasseh his father was in the hands of the enemy.","From the exile of Jehoiachin to the Destruction, eleven years; from the Destruction to Jehoiachin's imprisonment, twenty years,","and from the day of his exile, thirty-one; and during the six following years Psalm 87 (for us 88) was put forth.","At the end of the seventh year Evil-Merodach brought Jehoiachin out of his prison and honored him,","and the people nicknamed him Neri, because the lamp [ner] of David, which they feared would be extinguished, shone in him.","Then Psalm 88 (for us 89) was put forth, to render thanks to God and to pray for the welfare of the people and the exaltation of the horn of their anointed.","When this Neri was set free, God granted him a son, Meshubael, called Shealtiel,","who seventeen years before the end of the Babylonian exile begot Berechiah.","This Berechiah, in the seventeenth year, when the Babylonian exile ended, was leader of the people,","and because of that rank he was called Zerubbabel (zeh rav Bavel, \"this is the master of Babylon\"), in the eighty-first year of the Babylonian exile and the seventieth of the Destruction.","Now the people had two kinds of authority: the leaders [negidim] of the house of David,","and the priests of the tribe of Levi, each authority by itself, until the days of the Hasmoneans.","As a record of these matters our Seventy Elders left us the following written account.","Jeshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with Berechiah Zerubbabel son of Meshubael son of Neri, who is Jehoiachin, came to Jerusalem in the first year of Cyrus,","and in the second year they laid the foundations at the word of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah.","But the building was delayed on account of the death of Darius Hystaspes, and he could not go to Darius, being occupied in the war of the Tamyritzi. ⚠","When Cyrus was killed, Ahasuerus Artaxerxes the First reigned in his place,","who fought against Artashat, the ally of the Tamyritzi, who was inciting the Assyrians, the Medes and the Persians to revolt. ⚠","This Ahasuerus resided in Babylon. And because the governors of the land of Syria wrote an accusation against the Jews,","this Jeshua, in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus, left Joiakim his son, also called Eli,","in the office of the high priesthood in his stead, and went to Ahasuerus;","but since he was then occupied in war, he did not lend an ear to his words.","When he had won the war and heard that the Jews had cut off the head of (9) Holofernes the general,","he issued a decree concerning the Temple, that it should not be built. At his death he left two sons who contended for the kingdom,","and in the seventh month Darius Longimanus, who had vowed to lift the obstruction of his father's decree,","was saved by God and became king. In his first year Jeshua the high priest returned to Jerusalem,","and at the word of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah he bestirred himself to build the Temple.","Thus Jeshua held his first high priesthood for thirty-six years,","and he wrote down (10) the deeds of Judith and decreed that a commemoration of the deliverance be held every year.","After his return, as stated, he resumed his high priesthood for twenty years,","which ended in the twentieth year of Darius Longimanus, he being then one hundred and thirty years old.","Then Joiakim his son returned a second time to his high priesthood for forty-eight years,","until the twelfth year of Ahasuerus Artaxerxes the Great; he wrote the Scroll of Esther and decreed the observance of Purim according to the writings that came to him from Mordecai, who lived eighteen years longer than (11) Isaac.","As third high priest Eliashib arose, for twenty-one years, until the thirty-third year of Artaxerxes the Great,","and it was he who first undertook to build the Sheep Gate (Ezra 2:3) of Jerusalem. ⚠","The fourth high priest was Joiada, twenty-three years (Neh. 2:4[?]); likewise Jonathan was priest twenty-three years, until the end of that Artaxerxes; and the last high priest under the Persians was the sixth, Jaddua, ten years. ⚠","Now of the princes of the house of Nathan, the first was Simeon, also called Joash;","after him Levi, also called Amaziah; after him Jeshua, also called Hezekiah;","after him Er, also called Manasseh; these were before the exile.","After the exile ended, Zerubbabel ruled first, fifty-eight years;","after him Rhesa Meshullam, sixty-six; after him Johanan son of Rhesa Meshullam, fifty-three;","after him Judah, called Hyrcanus the First, fourteen. The high priests from Alexander to the Hasmoneans, up to Judah, were these:","Onias the First, twenty-seven years; Simeon the First, (12) thirteen;","Eleazar, enemy of Antiochus Theos, (13) twenty years; Manasseh, beloved of Seleucus Callinicus, twenty-seven;","Simeon the Righteous, who was honored by Antiochus the Great, twenty-eight;","Onias his son, in whose days (14) Seleucus despoiled the Temple, thirty-nine.","After this arose Judah Maccabee. But the princes of the house of David up to the said Judah were: Joseph the First, seven years;","Abner Shammai, eleven; Eli Mattathias, twelve;","Asar Maath, nine; Naggai Artashat, ten; Haggai Eli, eight;","Meshullot Nahum, seven; Amos Sirach, fourteen; Mattathias Shiloah, ten;","Joseph the Second, Arses, who was honored by Ptolemy, sixty; Jannai, who is Hyrcanus the Second, sixteen. ⚠","Afterwards the Hasmoneans arose and drew to themselves the rule of the house of David together with the high priesthood,","on which account enmity and jealousy were aroused; and Judah the Hasmonean, who raised his spear against Antiochus the Illustrious (that is, Epiphanes, which in Latin means illustris),","and against his son Eupator, and also against Demetrius, ruled five years;","Jonathan his brother, nineteen; Simeon, to whom Antiochus Sidetes granted remission of taxes,","ruled eight years; John Hyrcanus the First, twenty-six years;","Aristobulus, one year; Jannaeus Alexander, twenty-seven; and his wife Alexandra, nine;","and the last Hyrcanus, thirty-four. When this Hyrcanus was captured by the Parthians and left behind his wife, his daughter, and Aristobulus his son,","then by command of the Romans and against the will of the Jews Herod was made king by force,","and took as wife the daughter of Hyrcanus who had been captured by the Parthians,","and decreed that Aristobulus, son of the said Hyrcanus, should be high priest, in order to win the heart of the people.","This wife of his, the daughter of Hyrcanus, bore him two sons.","In the twenty-sixth year of his reign by force he heard that Hyrcanus his captive father-in-law was returning to his people and that the Jews were bowing down to him, as was the custom toward their former king,","and he killed this father-in-law of his, his mother-in-law, their daughter who was his wife, and the two sons she had borne him;","he also killed Aristobulus the high priest, and greatly oppressed the Jews for two years after these events.","In the thirtieth year of his reign by force he killed the Sanhedrin, who were of the house of David,","and chose a recorder and a Sanhedrin from the remnant of the people, those who appeared most learned.","He also killed Salome his sister and her husband, who was of the tribe of Judah.","Then the Jews grew weary of opposing him and of their own free will gave him the kingdom,","and swore allegiance also on behalf of his descendants after him. This Herod of Ashkelon reigned by force thirty-one years,","and a further six years with the consent of the Jews. After him Archelaus his son, nine;","after him Herod the Tetrarch, (15) twenty-four; and I, Yedidyah the Alexandrian, in the twenty-first year of his reign, was sent from Alexandria while still a youth (16) to plead on behalf of my brethren the Jews.","After this Herod, Agrippa the First reigned seven years,","after him Agrippa the Second, twenty-seven; after him Agrippinus, who was the last Agrippa, thirty years, up to this present year, the last of my old age. Thus far the words of Yedidyahu."],"notes":[{"seg":5,"he":"מלכים ב' ה'","note":"The sons of Bathsheba are listed in 2 Samuel 5:14 (counted as '2 Kings' in the Vulgate/Septuagint numbering of Samuel–Kings) and 1 Chr 3:5."},{"seg":8,"he":"אחי השר ומתת (מלכים א' ד')","note":"Pseudo-Philo (Annius of Viterbo's forgery) exploits Ahishar of 1 Kgs 4:6 and Nathan's sons in 1 Kgs 4:5; 'Mattat' plays on Nathan 'given'. Names transliterated."},{"seg":12,"he":"אך בלתי מעלת הכנסה","note":"Sense uncertain: perhaps 'without rank or revenue' (Latin original likely 'sine dignitate'). The parenthetical numerals here and below are the author's note markers."},{"seg":39,"he":"הטאמירי\"צי","note":"Unidentified people in the Latin pseudo-Philo; possibly related to Tomyris/Massagetae. Transliterated."},{"seg":41,"he":"ארת\"שת","note":"Unidentified figure from the Annian text; transliterated."},{"seg":58,"he":"עזרא ב' ג'","note":"The Sheep Gate is in Nehemiah 3:1, i.e. 'Second Ezra' ch. 3 in Vulgate numbering; reference kept as given."},{"seg":59,"he":"(נ\"ח ב\"ד)","note":"Parenthesis unclear and unbalanced in the printing; possibly a reference to Nehemiah. Kept as printed."},{"seg":74,"he":"ארסים","note":"Epithet uncertain (Arses?); the names in this list come from the Annian forgery's genealogy and are transliterated."}]}
